nodes.description: NFI-dependent programs of glial differentiation, axon outgrowth and midline guidance are required to build the corpus callosum and other commissures; their disruption yields a thin, hypoplastic, or absent corpus callosum. Nfia-null mice and nfia-null zebrafish show callosal agenesis and loss of commissural axons, respectively.

nodes.description: Nfia is expressed in the developing ureter and metanephric mesenchyme and is required in a dosage-sensitive manner for ureteral and renal development; its loss produces abnormalities of the ureteropelvic and ureterovesical junctions with vesicoureteral reflux and secondary hydronephrosis. Urinary involvement is incompletely penetrant, hence "with or without" urinary tract defects.

nodes.description: NFIA is necessary and sufficient to initiate gliogenesis in ventricular-zone progenitors and to maintain inhibition of neurogenesis; reduced NFIA impairs the switch from neurogenesis to gliogenesis and the migration/differentiation of astrocyte precursors that build CNS midline and ependymal structures. The causal links from this cellular defect to the corpus callosum and cerebrospinal fluid phenotypes are inferred from model-organism data (spinal-cord gliogenesis and Nfia-knockout callosal agenesis); direct human midline-glia evidence is limited.

nodes.description: NFIA is a sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription factor of the nuclear factor I family; its MH1 domain binds a nucleotide consensus in target promoters and the CTF_NFI domain regulates transcription. A reduced dose lowers NFIA-dependent transcriptional output at target genes governing CNS and urinary-tract development.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic Spectrum of NFIA Haploinsufficiency: Two Additional Cases and Review of the Literature.
